root_cause_note: Seventh crop of one class. The guard is being widened reactively, one prose SHAPE at a time; each widening catches the previous crop and misses the next publication SITE. R32 and R33 are outside the scanned set entirely (README) or outside the matched shapes (INDEX's ADR-019 entry, ADR-029's Consequences bullet). The untried structural move is to enumerate publication SITES rather than shapes: any CI-ceiling-like number in README, INDEX or specs/ must be struck, or must live in ADR-019 section 5 or the workflow.

findings.claim: R24 is not closed: README.md still publishes the retired CI `fast` ceiling (90s) as the live one, and repeats the 'measured at a different case count than this tree' disclaimer that ADR-019 struck in this very diff — so the top-level artifact contradicts its own table 85 lines below, and the workflow.
findings.evidence: README.md:99-100 — "CI's ceiling is the slowest observed run plus 15% (90s since ADR-019 section 5, measured on CI — at the case count of the commit named there, not this one)". Present tense, unstruck. README.md:184 in the same file publishes "so **25s** and **125s**", and .github/workflows/eval.yml:39 declares 125. Both halves of README:99 are false: the number, and the 'not this one' qualifier — run 32937020758 measured 14a6a7b at 213 fast / 74 invariant, this tree exactly. ADR-019's own 'smaller tree' paragraph asserting the same thing was struck 2026-08-26 as no longer true (ADR-019:63-70). The new scan cannot see it: it reads only specs/decisions/*.md, and only lines naming an EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_* variable or the literal 'CI ... stays N'. README:99's shape matches neither. Confirmed independently by the orchestrator.
findings.repro: grep -n "CI's ceiling is the slowest" README.md ; sed -n '184p' README.md ; grep -n 'EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST' .github/workflows/eval.yml
findings.acceptance: README:99 struck in place with a dated pointer, or rewritten to defer to ADR-019 section 5 as README:87 and ADR-019 section 7 now do; plus one case that could have gone red on it, watched red against the current README:99 before the sentence is edited.

findings.claim: Two more ungraded publishers of the retired CI ceilings survive unstruck inside the two documents R24 named — INDEX.md's ADR-019 entry and ADR-029's own Consequences bullet — so the digest whose header says 'what is now true' still says CI is 90/20, and ADR-029 contradicts its own section 2.
findings.evidence: INDEX.md:28 — the ADR-019 entry still reads "CI `fast` 80 -> 90, CI `invariant` 20", unchanged from `main`, unstruck, with an amendment trail naming only ADR-021 and not ADR-029 — while INDEX.md:30's ADR-021 entry WAS struck for the identical claim. ADR-029:140-144 — "Local and CI now publish different `fast` ceilings (105 vs 90) ... it is nonetheless the first time local has been the LOOSER of the two, which is a reason to re-derive CI's promptly rather than to leave it" — CI is now 125, local 105 is the TIGHTER of the two, and section 2 of that same file re-derived it. tasks/reviews/pr57-r6-resolution.json lists five struck sites and neither of these. Both are invisible to the new scan (no EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_* token, no 'CI ... stays N'). ADR-029:140-144 confirmed independently by the orchestrator.
findings.acceptance: Both struck in place with dated pointers (INDEX.md:28's entry also gaining ADR-029 in its amendment trail), and the scan widened to the shape that hid them — a CI ceiling asserted with the suite named in prose rather than by variable — demonstrated red on today's INDEX.md:28 before the strike lands.

findings.claim: The third of the three new prose-guard asserts is decorative: it re-types the pattern instead of exercising the one the guard uses, so a regression in the guard's own regex leaves it green.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:5439 asserts against a fresh literal pattern, while the loop at :5442 builds its own equivalent. Nothing ties them. By contrast `live`/`stays` (:1300, :1308) and `_SECONDS` (:5383) are compiled once and shared with their asserts — the reviewer confirmed those three DO fire when the lookahead is regressed to `(?![\d.])`. The comment at :5434-5438 claims the assert 'records that as a checked fact rather than an assumption'; it records a fact about a copy.
findings.repro: Compare the literal at eval_adapter.py:5439 with the pattern built at :5442 — editing the latter does not trip the former.
findings.acceptance: Compile the pattern once per suite and have the assert call that object, as the two sibling guards already do.

findings.claim: Named debt in the new anchors, confirmed rather than hypothetical: `stays` is suite-blind and accepts a wrong CI ceiling that equals the other suite's, and `live`'s 60-character window can grab an ADR number as if it were a ceiling.
findings.evidence: eval_adapter.py:1308 — `stays.findall("CI's `invariant` ceiling stays 125.")` grades 125 as green because 125 is declared for `fast`; only the variable-anchored shape is suite-aware. eval_adapter.py:1300 — `live.findall('`EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST` — see ADR-019 section 5 — is 125')` returns ('FAST','19') and would redden the gate on the ADR number. Neither fires today (zero matches across all 31 decision docs after strike-stripping, so the 'zero false positives' claim is true but vacuous), but ADR-002-performance-thresholds.md:4 already has both variables and digits on one line ~110 characters apart — one editing pass shorter and it reddens on '019'.
findings.repro: Run the two compiled patterns against the two strings above.
findings.acceptance: Either name the two holes in the guard's comment as declared ceilings (suite-blindness, and the window's ADR-number hazard) so the next reader is not surprised, or make `stays` read the suite word when the line carries one. No behaviour change required today.
